dedupe_keys.name: open wireless digital twin openairinterface with sionna rt ray tracing

description: The Open Wireless Digital Twin (OWDT) is an end-to-end wireless digital twin platform for evaluating mobile communication systems, built from open-source software and open data. It integrates OpenAirInterface (OAI) for 5G New Radio protocol stack emulation with NVIDIA Sionna RT for high-resolution ray-tracing-based propagation modelling, and adds OAI FlexRIC, an implementation aligned with the O-RAN near-real-time RAN Intelligent Controller, to monitor key performance indicators dynamically. The platform runs on a CPU-based Linux system and uses real-world building data; the authors evaluated it in urban mobility scenarios and report that it replicates real-world communication dynamics with high fidelity. Producer: a Japanese research team, with the arXiv paper submitted on 15 March 2025 and revised on 12 October 2025 and the journal version in IEEE Access. Coverage: urban areas for which building data exist. Access: the abstract page gives the paper only; whether the software is downloadable was not confirmed, so open_source is recorded as false meaning no verified open-source release. Licence and cost: not stated for the software; the paper is free and it is under the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Caveats: results come from urban test scenarios described in the paper, and Sionna RT requires a compatible setup. Simulation uses: it supports digital twin experiments, capacity planning and network optimisation of 5G radio access before deployment. Related records: the OpenAirInterface RF simulator (model-openairinterface-rf-simulator) and the NVIDIA Aerial Omniverse Digital Twin (platform-nvidia-aodt).
